kurz: Every appliance gets heat into food in its own way: by contact, hot air, radiation, steam or microwaves. Knowing this explains why the same recipe turns out differently.
bild_im_kopf: Like different trails up the same mountain: the summit is the same, but pace and view differ.
was_passiert: A pan passes on heat by direct contact, an oven through hot air and radiation. A steamer uses condensing steam, a microwave heats the water inside the food itself. Material and mass decide how much heat a tool stores and how fast it releases it.
warum_wichtig: Many failures are not down to the recipe but to the equipment: a thin pan cools down when searing, an air fryer browns faster than the oven.
faustregeln: For a crust: lots of mass and lots of heat, so a heavy pan, a pizza steel or hot cast iron.
For delicate things like eggs and fish: a pan that reacts fast and doesn't stick.
Treat recipes written for another appliance as a starting point and check earlier.
